messages:
Cassie: FYI Vega Health onboarding - monitoring flagged a weekly uptime drop to 99.2% vs contract SLO 99.9%. Possible credit question from customer. Can we gather evidence and decide external comms? /cc @Jordan @Priya
Jordan: Ack. Do we have an estimate of $$ exposure if monthly ends up below SLO? Need numbers to assess renewal risk.
Priya: I can pull metrics. Quick question - contract uses rolling 30d, right? This alert is from a weekly check. Which window should we use for the customer-facing calc?
Cassie: Contract SLO = rolling 30d. The customer saw the weekly noise and flagged it. For internal decision we need: final 30d uptime, last 7d for context, per-route latency p95, and incident timeline.
Liam: @Priya I can check infra logs and container events. Quick PromQL I usually run for uptime: `sum_over_time(up{customer="vega"}[30d]) / (30*24*3600)` - will also hit our uptime pipeline to confirm.
onboard-bot: VegaHealth onboarding status updated -> "warning: potential SLO breach" :warning: (automated check)
Priya: Running the queries now, pasting raw outputs in a moment.
Priya: Preliminary numbers: 30d observed uptime (service-probe) = 99.91% (still above 99.9), last 7d = 99.18%. Looks like a short-lived dip drove the alert but monthly window may be ok. Re-running with per-route filter.
Liam: Found infra events last Thursday - renderer pool 3 had repeated OOM restarts during a traffic spike. Incident INC-4789 created by deploy-bot. That aligns with the 7d dip.
Cassie: Good catch. Action items: (1) Priya to produce final monthly uptime calc + per-route p95 latency by EOD; (2) Liam to compile incident timeline + remediation summary; (3) Jordan to draft a customer note that explains weekly noise vs contract calc and a potential credit estimate. Review at 16:00.
Jordan: Drafting the note. Plan: 1) Quick summary of what we measured, 2) why contract uses 30d rolling SLO, 3) incident summary and fix, 4) optional credit calc/estimate if applicable. Tone: factual, avoid overpromising.
Cassie: Agreed. Example credit formula in the contract is: `Credit = min(0.5 * monthly_fee, ((SLO - observed_uptime) / SLO) * monthly_fee)`. Jordan, use this for estimates and flag legal if it looks material.
Jordan: Will do. Estimating exposure now given current numbers. If 30d stays at 99.91% there is no credit; if it drops to 99.5% that'll be X% of monthly_fee (I'll compute).
Priya: Finalized numbers: 30d uptime (service-probe): 99.91% - no credit triggered by contract. 7d uptime: 99.18% - explains customer's alert. Per-route p95 for API-ingest = 120ms, renderer = 680ms during the incident window. Attached query outputs below:
```
# uptime probe output (service-probe)
30d: 0.9991
7d: 0.9918
# per-route p95 samples
api-ingest_p95_ms: 120
renderer_p95_ms: 680 (spike window)
```
Liam: Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4789 - root cause: OOM on renderer pool 3 due to a recent config change + traffic spike. Fix: memory cap increased and autoscaler tuned.
Cassie: Thanks. Jordan - draft should call out that weekly probe noise is expected sometimes; confirm that contract calc is monthly rolling and current 30d meets SLO. Offer to run a one-off deeper latency review and show them dashboard graphs.
Jordan: Sending the customer note now (brief). I'll include a short appendix with the credit calc example and offer a 30-minute walkthrough with our enablement team.
Cassie: Please keep the language proactive: explain what we saw, why it didn't trigger a contract credit, what we fixed, and what we will do to reduce weekly noise (autoscaling, additional probes).
Jordan: Sent. Subject line: "Vega Health - SLO check & follow-up on recent noise". Copying CS enablement for the walkthrough.
Cassie: Great. Renewal risk: low for now - monitor next two weeks. If uptime drifts, we'll revisit credit exposure and loop in legal + finance.
Liam: I've scheduled a short runbook update to avoid recurrence. Will ping when it's live.
Cassie: Resolving the immediate ask. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
